about: I'm a Computational Data Science student at Penn State and a founder working where AI, product and business meet. From an Arabic-first legal workspace to computer-vision pipelines and workflow automation, I turn user problems into prototypes, test them with real people and work to make them useful. The question I keep coming back to is how to turn technically promising ideas into products people trust, use and pay for.
goals: Move Wathiq AI from early traction to reliable, recurring customer adoption
Build auditable, Arabic-first AI workflows that are tested with real users
Complete my B.S. in Computational Data Science at Penn State (expected May 2027)
Start more companies around overlooked business problems, and support research commercialization in Saudi Arabia

startups.title: Wathiq AI
startups.summary: An Arabic-first legal workspace for Saudi law firms that brings matters, tasks, documents and AI-assisted legal search with citations into one product.
details: Led 73+ interviews with practicing lawyers to map their workflows and pain points
Led 10+ AI and product features from concept to soft launch; not every feature is fully deployed
60+ lawyers in the pilot program and 110 registrations of interest, which are not paying customers
Raised an SAR 100K equity investment from a Saudi law firm after pitching to its lawyers in person

case.problem: Saudi legal teams juggle fragmented tools and manual work for matters, deadlines, documents and research, and general AI tools are weak in Arabic and hard to verify.
case.approach: I interviewed 73+ practicing lawyers, mapped their workflows, turned the findings into product specs, and coordinated developers through prototypes, model testing and feature releases.
case.evidence: 60+ lawyers in the pilot program, 110 registrations of interest, and an SAR 100K equity investment from a Saudi law firm.
case.next: Move from soft rollout to reliable, recurring adoption by law firms, measured by time saved, error rate and willingness to pay.

projects.title: Video Understanding Pipeline
projects.summary: A staged pipeline that turns video into readable scene summaries instead of captioning every frame.
details: YOLOv11n selects informative frames, Florence-2 captions them, and Command R+ writes the scene summary
Built in Python during KAUST's AI Summer Program

case.problem: Captioning every frame of a video is costly and loses the story across scenes.
case.approach: A staged pipeline: YOLOv11n picks informative frames, Florence-2 captions them, and Command R+ combines the captions into a readable scene summary.
case.evidence: Built as a team project during 320 hours of graduate-level AI training at KAUST.
case.next: Publish sample summaries and measure speed and accuracy before making performance claims.

projects.title: Arabic Corporate Writing QA System
projects.summary: An AI writing workflow that drafts and edits Arabic corporate documents, checked by a deterministic linter.
details: Writer and editor agents run through an /arabic-doc workflow
ar_lint.py has 807 lines, 34 rules and 28 self-tests, modeled on writing patterns from 10 Saudi organizations
Built with AI assistance (Claude), with every rule covered by tests

case.problem: AI-written Arabic corporate text often mixes terminology, slips out of the right register and adds unsupported superlatives.
case.approach: Writer and editor agents draft and revise documents, and a deterministic linter with 34 rules and 28 self-tests checks the result against writing patterns from 10 Saudi organizations.
case.evidence: Applied to the firm's company profile, including 45 Arabic consistency and grammar corrections in one revision.
case.next: Extend the rules and tests as new document types come in.

faq.a: Wathiq AI is an Arabic-first legal workspace for Saudi law firms. I co-founded it in August 2025 and lead it as CEO. It brings matters, tasks, documents and AI-assisted legal search with citations into one product, and it is in a soft rollout with pilot lawyers.

I'm drawn to the zero-to-one stage: finding an overlooked operational problem, talking to real users, building a working prototype and testing whether people will adopt it. The question I keep coming back to is how to turn technically promising ideas into products people trust, use and pay for.
I study at Penn State in State College, Pennsylvania, and my startup and consulting work is in Saudi Arabia.
